issue: Does the MVRA's automatic prison-trust-account turnover provision, 18 U.S.C. § 3664(n), reach outside deposits that are individually small but accumulate into a substantial sum over time, or only resources that are substantial when received?

sides.position: Section 3664(n) reaches resources that accumulate from periodic deposits into a substantial amount, not only resources that are substantial when received; the statute is not limited to windfalls.
cases: United States v. Myers, No. 23-1034 (9th Cir. 2026)
United States v. Kidd, 23 F.4th 781 (8th Cir. 2022)
United States v. Carson, 55 F.4th 1053 (6th Cir. 2022)
United States v. Elwood, 757 F. App'x 731 (10th Cir. 2018) (unpublished)

sides.position: Section 3664(n) applies only to windfalls, or to resources that are substantial at the time of receipt; small deposits that accumulate over time are not covered and must be analyzed transaction by transaction.
cases: United States v. Hughes, 914 F.3d 947 (5th Cir. 2019)
United States v. Saemisch, 70 F.4th 1 (1st Cir. 2023)

this_court: The Ninth Circuit panel majority takes the accumulation position: § 3664(n) can reach aggregated periodic deposits that become substantial, and it expressly disagrees with the First Circuit's windfall-only reading.
quote: As the panel dissent noted, the "substantial at the time of receipt" approach rejects the First and Fifth Circuit's construction of the statute.
cite: United States v. Myers, No. 23-1034 (9th Cir. 2026)
